title: Monthly Retail Trade benchmark revision — retail sales and inventories restated on the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey
source: EST: two Census primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06. census.gov/retail/index.html (HTTP 200, 742,392 bytes), verbatim: "Intention to Revise: Monthly retail estimates are anticipated to be revised based on historical corrections and the results of the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey. Revised not adjusted estimates and corresponding adjusted estimates are tentatively scheduled for release on September 28, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. EDT." Corroborated on census.gov/mtis/index.html (HTTP 200, 683,571 bytes): "...tentatively scheduled for release on September 28, 2026 and October 26, 2026, respectively. Revisions to the retail estimates are anticipated to be reflected in the August 2026 MTIS release scheduled for October 15, 2026." Filed estimate: Census's own word is "tentatively", the date is ABSENT from census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html (179 rows parsed, 2026-09-06), and the lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the mwts-benchmark-revision-2026-10-26 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06), on the MTIS announcements page that dates both halves of the same AIES restatement in one sentence. Why it earns a row rather than a footnote, and why it is the more consequential of the pair. (1) It is the DRESS REHEARSAL for the proposing event, 28 days earlier: both are 'tentatively scheduled', both are absent from the Census release calendar, both consume the same two AIES vintages (2023 AIES released 2026-02-26, 2024 AIES 2026-09-03), and the same page carries a Special Notice that M3 revised historical data and seasonal adjustment models "will remain unchanged for the remainder of 2026" for "schedule and resource constraints". Whether Census hits 09-28 is therefore the single best dated observation about whether it hits 10-26 — the proposing ledger registers a forward test on exactly that. (2) The retail series is the one this book's tracked calendar already treats as HIGH impact (retail-sales-2026-10-15, retail-sales-2026-11-17), so a restatement of its history is a larger object than the wholesale one; impact is filed MEDIUM rather than LOW on that ground, while still carrying no symbols and no macro-keyed playbook. (3) Its downstream date is stated by Census: the restated retail estimates are anticipated in the August-2026 MTIS release of 2026-10-15, which this calendar does not track (the tracked retail-sales-2026-10-15 is the 08:30 Advance Monthly Retail Trade report for SEPTEMBER data — different release, different hour, different reference month). Measured base rates from the proposing lane's own vintage study, offered as priors and NOT as claims about the retail series: across 12 wholesale benchmark revisions 2014-2025, all 12 restated 126+ historical months, at a median 0.126% per month. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry, and a restatement of the past carries no consensus to surprise against.
